acceptance: A reproduction or log evidence names the signal sender.
A test shows a lock waiter below a small memory threshold is not terminated under pressure level 2, or is restarted transparently.
A terminated preflight writes a failure record naming the signal and the phase.
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-26 `make pr-preflight` in BenchBox.wt-parquet-v2 was terminated by SIGTERM (rc 143, `make: *** [pr-preflight] Terminated: 15`) three times while waiting on the host test lock; once after its pytest step had passed (5,730 passed), leaving no receipt. The sentinel log at 15:06 shows pressure level 2 with the waiting `host_lock run --phase linux-preflight` process (0.06 GiB) listed among candidates. A waiter that uses almost no memory should not be killed, and a killed preflight should leave a clear failure record.

## Change
Find which component sent the signal (heavy sentinel, heavy-run watchdog, or lock-wait timeout) from ~/.benchbox/sentinel.log and the lock code; exempt idle lock waiters from memory-pressure kills or make them retry; make preflight report the cause on termination.

## Decision gates
- If the sentinel is not the sender, record the real sender before changing anything.
- Do not weaken the memory budget or disable the watchdog; owner approval is needed for any change to kill policy.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, make agent-write-preflight); the primary clone is read-only.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run; never bypass or signal the lock, and never kill processes by name pattern (pkill -f); stop only PIDs you started.
- Commits as the configured human identity; no agent attribution.
- No carried or own reimplementation of upstream code without the owner decision recorded in datagen-decision-upstream-gap-policy.
- A choice between a small and a large implementation path goes to the owner with sizes before work starts.
- Report only results that were observed; name anything not run.
